problemFraming.currentState: CJTF-WestPac has been activated with operational control of naval, air, ground, and special operations component forces in the Western Pacific. PLA Eastern Theater Command has initiated military operations including naval blockade of Taiwan's eastern ports, air incursions into Taiwan's ADIZ, and ballistic missile strikes against military installations. Allied forces are dispersed across forward bases in Japan, Guam, and the Philippines but face A2/AD threats during force concentration. Coalition partners have committed forces but integration and interoperability gaps remain.
problemFraming.desiredEndState: PLA force projection across the Taiwan Strait denied; CJTF-WestPac maintains air and maritime superiority in the Philippine Sea and Western Pacific approaches; Taiwan's ability to sustain defense operations preserved through sea and air lines of communication; coalition forces integrated under unified C2 with demonstrated interoperability; conditions set for conflict termination on terms favorable to the alliance.
problemFraming.problemStatement: How does CJTF-WestPac integrate joint and combined forces to deny PLA cross-strait power projection, maintain air and maritime superiority, and preserve Taiwan's defense capability within acceptable risk to coalition forces?
keyTensions: Force concentration for decisive operations vs dispersal for survivability against A2/AD
Aggressive offensive action vs risk management for high-value platforms (carriers, amphibs)
Speed of coalition integration vs thoroughness of interoperability verification
Offensive counter-A2/AD operations vs defensive protection of sea lines of communication
Munitions conservation for sustained operations vs mass employment for rapid effect
obstacles: PLA DF-21D and DF-26 anti-ship ballistic missiles threaten carrier strike group operations within 1,500nm
PLA submarine force (60+ boats) complicates sea control in the Philippine Sea
Limited joint munitions stockpiles — estimated 7-14 day supply of precision-guided munitions
Electromagnetic spectrum congestion degrades coalition C2 in contested environment
Taiwan Strait geography constrains maneuver options for surface forces
opportunities: PLA amphibious forces must concentrate at predictable embarkation points along Fujian coast
Japanese MSDF expertise in ASW provides critical submarine defense capability
Distributed maritime operations (DMO) can complicate PLA targeting across wide areas
PLA logistics chain across Taiwan Strait is vulnerable to interdiction
Allied undersea advantage (Virginia-class, Astute-class) enables offensive ASW deep in PLA waters
assumptions: Carrier strike groups can operate effectively from standoff ranges of 500-1000nm
Japanese MSDF provides ASW screen in the Ryukyu Island chain and Philippine Sea
Air refueling capacity sufficient to sustain combat air patrols from Guam and mainland Japan
Submarine-launched cruise missiles available for initial strikes against PLA C2 nodes
Taiwan military maintains coherent defense for minimum 14 days without external resupply
constraints: Carrier operations restricted to east of Ryukyu Island chain until A2/AD degraded
Coalition ROE requires positive identification before engagement of maritime contacts
No strikes on PRC mainland without explicit national command authority authorization
Nuclear facilities, civilian population centers, and Three Gorges Dam are restricted targets
Submarine operations zones must deconflict with allied submarine water space management

children.label: Undersea Warfare Dominance

children.description: Minimum 8 SSNs on station for barrier patrols, ASW, and offensive strike missions

children.label: SSN Maintenance Backlog
children.description: Submarine maintenance delays limit available boats; loss of even 1-2 SSNs significantly degrades coverage

root.label: PLA Cross-Strait Assault Capability
root.description: Eastern Theater Command's ability to project ground forces across the Taiwan Strait through coordinated amphibious, airborne, and fires operations

children.label: Amphibious Lift and Landing
children.description: Capacity to transport and land 1st echelon forces (80,000+ troops) on Taiwan's western beaches within 48 hours

children.label: Protected Sealift Corridors
children.description: Cleared sea lanes from Fujian embarkation ports to Taiwan landing beaches, defended against allied submarine and surface threats

children.label: Chokepoint Vulnerability
children.description: Amphibious forces must transit narrow corridors predictable from beach gradient analysis — targetable by submarines and land-based anti-ship missiles

children.label: Fires Suppression of Taiwan Defenses
children.description: Short-range ballistic missile (DF-11/DF-15) and cruise missile strikes to suppress Taiwan air defenses, C2 nodes, and port facilities

children.label: Real-Time Battle Damage Assessment
children.description: Rapid BDA to confirm suppression effects and retarget surviving Taiwan defense assets

children.label: BDA Latency
children.description: Cloud cover and Taiwan denial/deception degrade satellite BDA; PLA may waste follow-on strikes on already-destroyed or decoy targets

linesOfEffort.name: Deny Cross-Strait Power Projection
linesOfEffort.description: Degrade and deny PLA ability to project forces across the Taiwan Strait through anti-surface warfare, mine warfare, and submarine interdiction of amphibious shipping

decisivePoints.label: Submarine Barrier Established
decisivePoints.description: SSN barrier patrols in Luzon Strait and east Taiwan approaches deny PLA submarine freedom of maneuver

decisivePoints.label: PLA Sealift Attrited Below Assault Threshold
decisivePoints.description: Combined submarine, surface, and air attacks reduce PLA amphibious lift capacity below viable assault levels

linesOfEffort.name: Achieve Air and Maritime Superiority
linesOfEffort.description: Establish local air superiority over the Philippine Sea and maritime superiority along sea lines of communication through offensive counter-air and surface warfare operations

decisivePoints.label: A2/AD Envelope Degraded
decisivePoints.description: Counterspace, electronic warfare, and standoff strikes degrade PLA IADS and ASBM targeting chain

decisivePoints.label: Air Superiority East of Taiwan
decisivePoints.description: CAP and BARCAP operations establish air superiority bubble east of Taiwan for logistics and force flow

linesOfEffort.name: Sustain Taiwan Defense Capability
linesOfEffort.description: Maintain sea and air lines of communication to Taiwan to enable resupply of critical military materials, munitions, and humanitarian supplies

decisivePoints.label: Eastern SLOC Secured
decisivePoints.description: Protected corridor from Philippine Sea to Taiwan east coast ports established and defended

decisivePoints.label: Critical Resupply Delivered
decisivePoints.description: Minimum 3 resupply convoys deliver air defense munitions, anti-ship missiles, and medical supplies

linesOfEffort.name: Integrate Coalition Forces
linesOfEffort.description: Achieve seamless C2 integration across US, Japanese, Australian, and Philippine naval and air forces for unified theater operations

decisivePoints.label: Coalition C2 Operational
decisivePoints.description: Shared COP, deconflicted water space management, and allied liaison officers integrated at CJTF-WP HQ

decisivePoints.label: Allied ASW Screen Active
decisivePoints.description: Japanese MSDF and Australian Navy ASW assets integrated into barrier defense with shared underwater picture

phases.name: Alert & Deploy
phases.description: CJTF-WestPac activates, disperses forces to distributed basing locations, establishes coalition C2, and begins ISR surge coverage of PLA military preparations.

phases.name: Seize Initiative
phases.description: Upon PLA hostile action, immediately execute counter-A2/AD strikes, establish submarine barriers, and begin degrading PLA ISR and targeting chain through counterspace and electronic warfare.

phases.name: Dominate
phases.description: Sustain high-tempo joint fires to attrit PLA amphibious capability below viable threshold. Establish air superiority east of Taiwan. Open and defend SLOC for Taiwan resupply operations.

phases.name: Conflict Termination
phases.description: Create conditions for ceasefire through demonstrated military superiority and PLA inability to sustain cross-strait operations. Support diplomatic resolution while maintaining combat posture.

decisionPoints.label: Commit Carrier Strike Groups
criteria: PLA ASBM targeting chain assessed as degraded
CSG escort screen at full strength with BMD Aegis assets
Commander accepts risk of operating within DF-26 range

decisionPoints.label: Open Taiwan SLOC
criteria: Air superiority established east of Taiwan
PLA submarine threat in eastern approaches reduced to acceptable level
Escort forces available for convoy protection

criteria: PLA cross-strait assault capability decisively degraded
Coalition forces can sustain operations without unacceptable attrition
Diplomatic conditions enable favorable ceasefire terms

operationalApproach.narrative: CJTF-WestPac executes a four-phase operational approach focused on denying PLA cross-strait power projection while preserving Taiwan's defense capability. Upon activation, the joint force disperses to distributed basing locations across Japan, Guam, and the Philippines to complicate PLA targeting. Coalition C2 integration and ISR surge provide early warning and shared situational awareness. When PLA initiates hostilities, CJTF-WP seizes the initiative through simultaneous counter-A2/AD operations — counterspace degradation of PLA ISR satellites, electronic warfare against over-the-horizon radars, and submarine-launched cruise missile strikes against key C2 nodes. Submarine barrier patrols in the Luzon Strait and eastern Taiwan approaches immediately threaten PLA amphibious shipping. As the A2/AD umbrella degrades, carrier strike groups commit from standoff positions in the Philippine Sea, generating sustained air sorties for offensive counter-air and anti-surface warfare. The Dominate phase concentrates joint fires on PLA sealift — targeting embarkation ports, convoy routes, and landing craft to attrit amphibious capacity below viable assault threshold. Simultaneously, coalition ASW forces (MSDF and Australian Navy) maintain the underwater barrier while surface forces secure eastern SLOCs for Taiwan resupply convoys. The operational approach converges on conflict termination conditions when PLA leadership recognizes that cross-strait assault is no longer feasible, creating diplomatic space for ceasefire negotiations that preserve Taiwan's de facto independence.
